claims.text: Advanced Monte Carlo methods can produce concurrent strength and ductility improvement in crystalline metals or alloys.
Enhanced sampling techniques can predict material properties relevant to strength and ductility.
The proposed method is applicable under ambient conditions.
Grain boundaries act as a structural mediator between applying Monte Carlo methods and improving strength and ductility.
Precipitates act as a structural mediator between applying Monte Carlo methods and improving strength and ductility.
Enhanced sampling of yield strength can help optimize strength and ductility simultaneously.
Enhanced sampling of strain hardening can help optimize strength and ductility simultaneously.
Traditional materials design exhibits a trade-off between strength and ductility.
Traditional alloying methods are limited in achieving concurrent strength and ductility improvement.
Traditional grain-refinement methods are limited in achieving concurrent strength and ductility improvement.
Traditional precipitation-hardening methods are limited in achieving concurrent strength and ductility improvement.
